public_contracts.name: default check (no flags)
public_contracts.detail: Whole-runtime read-only check; byte-identical MATCH/DIFF output and the same exit codes as the base commit. A missing installation still reports MATCH and exits 0.

public_contracts.name: --print-manifest / --import-from / --canonical / --destination
public_contracts.detail: Parsing, output and behaviour are untouched. Combining either of them with --file or --json is now a usage error (exit 2) raised before any write.

public_contracts.name: public functions installable_files / manifest / installation_diff / sync_installation / import_installation / unique_destinations / main
public_contracts.detail: Every positional signature is unchanged and locked by test_old_public_callers_keep_their_signatures. sync_installation now returns its per-target result dict instead of None and still raises OSError when any file could not be written, so library callers keep the old fail-loud contract.

public_contracts.name: installable_files(canonical) runtime closure
public_contracts.detail: Still 75 files (3 root files + agents/config/references/scripts). tools/ and tools/tests/ are not in the manifest and are never copied into a user skill installation.

public_contracts.name: --file <relative> (repeatable)
public_contracts.detail: New. Restricts check, --plan and --apply to a normalized, de-duplicated, sorted subset of installable_files(canonical). Absolute paths, '..', directory names, out-of-closure paths and target-escaping links are rejected with exit 2 and zero writes at every destination.

public_contracts.name: --plan
public_contracts.detail: New. Zero-write plan emitted as exactly one rf-install-plan/1 JSON value on stdout; exit 0 when the plan is produced, exit 2 only on a validation error. Per target/relative it carries operation (new|replace|unchanged), before_sha256 or null, source_sha256, size, plus selected_drift and unselected_drift counts. It may report 'new' for a missing installation even though the default check still reports no drift there. It is machine fact, never a receipt or an eligibility gate, and no plan file is required before --apply.

public_contracts.name: rf-install-result/1 (--json)
public_contracts.detail: New. Exactly one JSON value on stdout with all diagnostics on stderr. Each target entry carries target/selected/written/unchanged/failed/conflicts/drifted/remaining_selected_drift/remaining_unselected_drift/status, with status in completed|partial|failed. Exit code is 1 exactly when remaining_selected_drift > 0, so unselected drift can never fail a completed selected sync and a clean subset never prints the whole-runtime MATCH.

public_contracts.name: per-file atomic replacement and failure reporting
public_contracts.detail: Files whose bytes already match are never staged, never os.replace'd and keep their mtime/size/content. Source and target are re-hashed immediately before each swap; a change on either side is reason='conflict' and the file is left alone. A failure returns exit 1 with accurate written/unchanged/failed/conflict lists, claims no whole-batch rollback, keeps no backup and no second transaction store, and a re-run against the current differences converges on the remainder while touching already-written files no further.

public_contracts.name: temporary-file ownership
public_contracts.detail: Only this invocation's own .<skill>-stage-<random>/ directory under destination and its <name>.<pid>.syncing siblings are created and cleaned; no glob ever removes another process's temporary files.
